rationale: Step 8 produced results/trivariate_var.json with okun.all_states = {coef: 18.270, t: 14.687, n: 714} and okun.farm_states = {coef: 14.667, t: 4.424, n: 126}. The paper's pooled Okun coefficient is ~-0.32 (t=17.5) and the farm-state coefficient ~-0.22 (t=8.1). The produced coefficients are wrong-signed and off by roughly two orders of magnitude: okun() in src/trivariate_var.py (lines 97-110) regresses Delta(rel_urate) — in percentage points — on Delta(rel_emp_logdev) — a log deviation where 0.01 = 1% — so the slope is ~100x the paper's per-percentage-point convention. Rescaling by /100 gives ~0.183 (pooled) and ~0.147 (farm), which are still 33-43% away from 0.32 and 0.22 and thus not even within the partial band; and the produced values as reported (18.27, 14.67) are nowhere near -0.32/-0.22. The t-stats also miss: typical t=14.69 vs 17.5 (~16% low) and farm t=4.42 vs 8.1 (~45% low). Additionally the coefficient is computed as a simple bivariate OLS of Delta-urate on Delta-emp rather than extracted from the trivariate VAR system the claim specifies. Only the qualitative ordering matches — the farm-state coefficient (14.67) is closer to zero than the pooled one (18.27), consistent with the paper — but the numeric magnitudes and signs do not match, so this is a no_match.
